record.paper_title: Open Problems in Understanding the Nuclear Chirality
record.context_brief: Microscopic collective Hamiltonian extension of PRM
record.original_question: Can the particle-rotor description of chiral doublet bands be reformulated so that the rigid core is replaced by a collective Hamiltonian whose parameters are extracted microscopically from constrained triaxial mean-field calculations, thereby incorporating vibration-rotation coupling into chirality studies in a genuinely microscopic way?

evidence.quote: The possible extension of the PRM is the replacement of the core by the collective Hamiltonian with the parameters extracted in a similar way, which may provide a new dimension in the description of the chiral doublet bands.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In nuclear structure, the particle–rotor model (PRM) describes a deformed odd–odd (or odd-A) nucleus as a system of valence quasi-particles (e.g. a quasi-proton and a quasi-neutron in a high-j shell) coupled to a rigid triaxial rotor core characterized by fixed deformation parameters (β, γ) and three rigid moments of inertia 𝒥_k (k=1,2,3). Diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonian
  H_PRM = Σ_k (R_k)^2/(2𝒥_k) + H_qp ,
where R = I − j is the core angular momentum and I, j are the total and valence-particle angular momenta, can produce nearly degenerate pairs of ΔI = 1 bands ("chiral doublet bands") that signal the spontaneous breaking of chiral symmetry by an aplanar angular-momentum geometry.

Problem. Replace the rigid triaxial rotor core in the PRM by a quantum collective Bohr-type Hamiltonian
  H_coll = T_vib(β, γ) + T_rot(β, γ; θ_i) + V(β, γ),
in which the kinetic mass tensor B_{ij}(β, γ), the moments of inertia 𝒥_k(β, γ), and the collective potential V(β, γ) are all functions of the deformation variables (β, γ), and these functions are determined microscopically from constrained self-consistent triaxial mean-field calculations (e.g. constrained Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov or relativistic mean-field calculations with constraints on the quadrupole deformations). Couple this collective core to the valence quasi-particles to obtain a microscopic particle-plus-collective Hamiltonian
  H = H_coll(β, γ) + H_qp + H_coupling ,
that explicitly accounts for vibration–rotation coupling in (β, γ) as well as for triaxial rotation.

Question. Does there exist such a microscopically founded particle-plus-collective formulation that (i) reduces to the standard PRM in the rigid-rotor limit, (ii) takes all of its (β,γ)-dependent inertia and potential parameters from constrained triaxial mean-field calculations without further phenomenological adjustment, and (iii) yields a quantitatively consistent description of observed chiral doublet bands (energy splittings, B(M1)/B(E2) ratios, and the influence of β- and γ-vibrational degrees of freedom) in candidate chiral nuclei?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works have made substantial progress on this program. A two-dimensional collective Hamiltonian on azimuth/polar motions, with potential and mass parameters from three-dimensional tilted axis cranking (TAC) mean-field calculations, has been developed and used to restore broken chiral/signature symmetries (Chen et al., and follow-ups). β-soft collective Hamiltonians coupled to chiral configurations and rotation-vibration models for chiral and wobbling bands have also appeared (e.g. Phys. Rev. C 110, 034301 (2024)). However, a fully (β,γ)-dependent microscopic particle-plus-collective Hamiltonian extension of PRM with all parameters extracted from constrained triaxial mean-field calculations and benchmarked systematically against chiral data is still being developed; the program is therefore partially realized rather than fully completed.

status_evidence.title: Rotation-vibration model for the chiral doublet bands and wobbling bands in transitional nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: A collective model Hamiltonian incorporating a β-soft potential is proposed to elucidate phenomena related to triaxiality... suggesting a collective vibration mechanism for multiple chiral doublet bands.
status_evidence.claim: Collective Hamiltonian with vibrational degrees of freedom has been used to study chiral doublet bands, indicating ongoing progress beyond the rigid-rotor PRM.

status_evidence.title: Collective Hamiltonian for chiral modes
status_evidence.snippet: Two-dimensional collective Hamiltonian (2DCH) with collective potential and mass parameters determined from three-dimensional tilted axis cranking (TAC) calculations.
status_evidence.claim: A microscopically based collective Hamiltonian for chiral modes with parameters from TAC mean-field calculations has been constructed, addressing key parts of the proposed extension.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic nuclear structure models and methods: Chiral symmetry, Wobbling motion and γ-bands
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic investigation using multi-quasiparticle triaxial projected shell model (TPSM) approach for chiral doublet bands and wobbling mode.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative microscopic frameworks (TPSM) have been applied to chiral doublet bands, indicating that the broader microscopic program is active and progressing.
